statusDetail: Coverage-complete audit of five representative route archetypes plus the download-options step.

page.framework: Server-rendered HTML/PHP-style templates with small inline JavaScript and third-party analytics/advertising
page.notes: Input host redirects through .latino, .fast, and .dad to https://www.mp4moviez.soccer/. Templates vary materially; the request route is legacy and lacks viewport meta.

artifacts.caption: Homepage under dark and reduced-motion preferences
Computed homepage styles under dark and reduced-motion preferences
Raw HTML versus rendered discoverability result
Semantics, forms, focus, motion, metadata, capability probe
Performance resources, memory, scripts, and permissions probe
HTTP statuses for robots, sitemap, and representative 404

checkOutcomes.method: Emulated dark-mode screenshot and computed styles
checkOutcomes.evidence: Screenshot and computed-style probe under prefers-color-scheme: dark show unchanged white surfaces and color-scheme: normal.
Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, getAnimations() returned an empty array; the tested templates have no automatic motion to suppress.
axe and Lighthouse report 80 insufficient-contrast nodes across links and form controls.
CSS/DOM inspection across same-origin route changes found no view-transition declarations or transition naming.
No scroll listeners, animation timelines, or running animations were found; scrolling remains native and does not add main-thread animation work.
The site relies on native scrolling and ordinary links, with no custom pointer/gesture interception that conflicts with platform behavior.
Very long home/search pages expose no progress, sticky context, or scroll-state affordance.
No tooltip, menu, popover, dialog, or other anchored overlay exists on the representative templates.
checkOutcomes.reason: No tooltip, menu, popover, dialog, or other anchored overlay exists on the representative templates.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Headings, alternating result rows, and the detail-page information/download headings visibly establish the next content state.
No full-viewport interruption appears on initial load of the home, listing, search, detail, or request templates.
Representative pages expose no user-visible dismissible overlay or disclosure component requiring dialog/popover/details semantics.
checkOutcomes.reason: Representative pages expose no user-visible dismissible overlay or disclosure component requiring dialog/popover/details semantics.

checkOutcomes.method: Visual review of desktop and mobile screenshots
checkOutcomes.evidence: The first viewport prioritises title, search, and latest content; there is no persistent sidebar or app chrome consuming the viewport.
Content templates fit 360px, but the request template lacks viewport meta and renders a 980px desktop canvas scaled down to 0.367.
No container queries were found and the request/list components do not adapt independently to narrow space.
Programmatic keyboard focus on the search input produced a visible browser outline (auto 1px); controls use native links/inputs.
The home, listing, search, detail, and download-options pages use explicit headings and labelled links that state their catalog/search purpose.

checkOutcomes.method: Walkthrough of search, detail, and download-options DOM
checkOutcomes.evidence: The search-to-detail flow reaches quality choices, but higher-quality download links add an undisclosed unrelated popup and hidden ad surfaces.
Empty search has no feedback, request leaves the site, and these flows provide no first-party status or recovery message.
Lighthouse measured FCP 4.4s and LCP 4.9s; CLS was 0 and TBT 10ms, so loading rather than stability/input is the failure.
Layout observers on home/listing/detail/search/request recorded CLS 0 with no shifts; Lighthouse also reported CLS 0.
Trace recorded no long tasks and 0ms total blocking time; Lighthouse TBT was 10ms.
HAR recorded 2.43MB with 2.25MB images, four redirects, and widespread eager/oversized image delivery.
Lighthouse estimated 66KiB unused JavaScript in the analytics payload.
axe reports a critical missing-label violation for #searchInput.
axe and Lighthouse report 80 WCAG AA color-contrast failures.

checkOutcomes.method: axe region audit and focus/landmark probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: Focus is visible, but axe reports footer content outside landmarks and no footer landmark exists.
Main templates use 13–15px text, while the request page is desktop-scaled to 0.367 on mobile, producing visibly tiny text.

checkOutcomes.method: Mobile layout and Lighthouse target audit
checkOutcomes.evidence: Request lacks viewport meta and fails mobile reflow; Lighthouse reports an insufficient touch target. No timed media requires captions.
Lighthouse errors-in-console audit scored 1 with no browser errors logged.
Doctype/charset are present, but Lighthouse reports 35 incorrect image aspect ratios and 40 unsized images.
Lighthouse passed doctype, deprecated API, console, HTTPS, and third-party-cookie checks; no permission prompt fires on load.
All representative content templates expose a non-empty title and meta description in server-rendered HTML.
Content links have real href values, robots.txt is valid, and main content templates include viewport meta; raw HTML exposes 100% of rendered content.

checkOutcomes.method: Metadata, sitemap, and HAR redirect inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: No canonical is present; the live .soccer destination conflicts with .scot sitemap URLs and follows four host redirects.
Open Graph/Twitter metadata exists, but the probe found zero JSON-LD blocks for catalog entities.

checkOutcomes.method: Security headers, cookies, and secrets probes
checkOutcomes.evidence: HTTPS is used, but all six tested defensive response-header families are missing.

checkOutcomes.method: Tracker, HAR, and download-template DOM inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: Analytics runs on load and download templates add numerous ad/player origins, tracking pixels, and a hidden iframe.
No permission request is made on load and the site exposes no authentication/account flow requiring WebAuthn.
CSP, frame controls, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, HSTS, and nosniff are absent despite risky third-party execution.
Discoverability comparison shows 100% raw-HTML content coverage and no JS shell; core navigation/content use ordinary links.

checkOutcomes.method: Raw-vs-rendered DOM and HAR error inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: Core catalog content and links are server-rendered and remain available independently of analytics/ad script success.
This is a navigational public catalog, not an installed application; no product intent indicates offline operation or installation.
checkOutcomes.reason: This is a navigational public catalog, not an installed application; no product intent indicates offline operation or installation.

checkOutcomes.method: Direct HTTP 404 fetch and body review
checkOutcomes.evidence: A tested missing route returns 404 but offers no navigation, search, retry, or recovery action.
lang is present, but a site claiming global/multilingual reach uses physical CSS and exposes no direction-safe logical properties or alternate-language links.
The tested en/en-in pages use an English textual date and do not expose currency, numeric input, or dynamic locale-sensitive calculations.
No event scheduling, live time, deadline, recurring interval, or user-entered time zone exists on the representative routes.
checkOutcomes.reason: No event scheduling, live time, deadline, recurring interval, or user-entered time zone exists on the representative routes.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Download links conceal popup side effects and the page injects an opacity 0.001 fixed iframe.
Empty search is silently cancelled with no message, invalid state, or focus recovery.
The search input has no name, label, autocomplete, or inputmode metadata.
No checkout, subscription, payment, account, sign-in, or cancellation flow is offered.
checkOutcomes.reason: No checkout, subscription, payment, account, sign-in, or cancellation flow is offered.

checkOutcomes.evidence: All 77 audited images are legacy formats; 36 are oversized and 37 lack responsive sources.
Seventy-four below-fold images load eagerly and analytics starts during initial navigation.
The load transfers 2.43MB and the full download route adds many ad/player dependencies with no visible budget or consent gate.
The site exposes a simple public document/search catalog with no declared agent-tool intent or authenticated task surface requiring WebMCP.
checkOutcomes.reason: The site exposes a simple public document/search catalog with no declared agent-tool intent or authenticated task surface requiring WebMCP.

checkOutcomes.evidence: No summarisation, generation, or inference feature is part of the site’s purpose; built-in AI integration would not advance its core task.
checkOutcomes.reason: No summarisation, generation, or inference feature is part of the site’s purpose; built-in AI integration would not advance its core task.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The audited site is a full-navigation MPA with no repeatable same-document interaction such as modal, SPA route, editor, or infinite list to exercise ten times.
checkOutcomes.reason: The audited site is a full-navigation MPA with no repeatable same-document interaction such as modal, SPA route, editor, or infinite list to exercise ten times.

checkOutcomes.method: Heap snapshot summary and Performance memory probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: Heap summary reports 4.79MB self size; runtime used JS heap is about 4.79MB with 578 DOM elements, proportionate to a static catalog page.

checkOutcomes.method: Heap constructor summary and runtime/DOM inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: The single-state heap summary contains no Detached constructor among reported top constructors, and the static MPA exposes no recurring timer/listener interaction.

principleOutcomes.reason: The site exposes a simple public document/search catalog with no declared agent-tool intent or authenticated task surface requiring WebMCP. No summarisation, generation, or inference feature is part of the site’s purpose; built-in AI integration would not advance its core task.

paths.description: Homepage and global template: entry purpose, latest items, search, preferences, performance, network, metadata, and security.
Bollywood category listing representing category/index templates.
Search results for “game”, representing the primary discovery flow and long result lists.
Game of Thrones detail page representing catalog detail/information templates.
Next step from the detail page, representing the primary download-choice flow; file transfer itself was not initiated.
Request Movies route representing the support/request journey and legacy template.

findings.summary: The site ignores the user’s dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot remains white, and computed body/header surfaces are rgb(255,255,255) with color-scheme: normal.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide prefers-color-scheme-aware surface and text tokens.

findings.summary: Color choices fail common contrast requirements.
findings.evidence: axe and Lighthouse both report 80 contrast failures, including featured links, the search input, and submit control.
findings.suggestedFix: Use tested semantic color tokens that meet WCAG AA and add a prefers-contrast/forced-colors treatment.

findings.summary: Navigation changes are abrupt across a long multi-page journey.
findings.evidence: DOM/CSS inspection found no view-transition declarations; listing, detail, and download-option navigations fully replace the page.
findings.suggestedFix: Use cross-document View Transitions for same-origin navigation with a no-motion fallback.

findings.summary: Long listings provide no scroll-position or progress cue.
findings.evidence: The homepage is about 9,914 CSS px tall and search results about 6,160 px; probe/CSS inspection found no scroll-state or progress affordance.
findings.suggestedFix: Add lightweight sticky context or a scroll progress/return-to-top affordance without obscuring content.

findings.summary: The request page is not mobile-responsive.
findings.evidence: At a 360x800 emulation the request page has no viewport meta and renders a 980 CSS px layout scaled to 0.367, making text and controls tiny.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a viewport meta tag and rebuild the template with a fluid, reflowing layout and readable mobile typography.

findings.summary: Components use one fixed presentation rather than adapting to available space.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found zero container queries; the request template falls back to desktop scaling and list rows keep fixed image dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Adopt intrinsic sizing and container queries for reusable list, header, and form components.

findings.summary: The primary download flow triggers undisclosed advertising behavior.
findings.evidence: The download-options DOM shows 480p/720p links with onclick window.open() to sb.inveilfunds.com, plus a hidden fixed iframe at opacity 0.001 and multiple ad scripts.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unsolicited popups and hidden frames; make each link perform only its stated action and disclose any external navigation.

findings.summary: Search and request actions lack clear validation and recovery states.
findings.evidence: The search form silently does nothing for an empty query, and the request page sends users to Facebook rather than presenting an in-page form or status/recovery message.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide inline status, empty/error messaging, and a recoverable first-party request flow.

findings.summary: Loading is slow despite a simple server-rendered page.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured FCP 4.4s and LCP 4.9s (performance 0.71); four sequential domain redirects alone have an estimated 3.52s saving.
findings.suggestedFix: Choose one canonical host, redirect directly once, and prioritise the LCP content.

findings.summary: Resource delivery is dominated by eager, oversized images.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 2.43 MB transferred, 2.25 MB images; the image audit found 74 below-fold images not lazy-loaded, 36 oversized, and 37 without srcset.
findings.suggestedFix: Lazy-load below-fold covers, serve responsive AVIF/WebP variants, and correctly prioritise only the LCP image.

findings.summary: Analytics JavaScript adds avoidable work and bytes.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 66 KiB unused JavaScript; HAR shows the 169.7 KiB Google tag is the largest script on a page whose core content needs no client rendering.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unnecessary analytics code or load a smaller consent-aware implementation after core content.

findings.summary: The search field has no accessible name.
findings.evidence: axe reports a critical label violation for #searchInput; the DOM has no label, aria-label, or aria-labelledby.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a visible <label> associated with the search input and preserve a meaningful input name.

findings.summary: Footer content sits outside landmarks.
findings.evidence: axe reports three region violations for .footer-cta, .footer-content, and .welcome; the probe found no footer landmark.
findings.suggestedFix: Wrap footer material in <footer> and keep heading/landmark structure consistent across templates.

findings.summary: The request template fails mobile reflow and target legibility.
findings.evidence: The request page has no viewport meta and is scaled from 980 CSS px at a 360px device width; Lighthouse also reports an insufficient touch target on the homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a correct viewport meta tag, fluid layout, and at least 24x24 CSS px spaced targets (prefer 44x44).

findings.summary: Many image elements have invalid sizing hygiene.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports 35 incorrect aspect ratios and 40 unsized images; the image probe independently reports 40 missing dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit correct width/height or aspect-ratio for every image and avoid stretching intrinsic ratios.

findings.summary: Canonical and sitemap signals disagree with the live URL.
findings.evidence: The live document has no rel=canonical; the webcam URL redirects through four hosts to .soccer, while sitemap.xml lists stale .scot URLs.
findings.suggestedFix: Select one canonical origin, update sitemap URLs, add self-referencing canonicals, and collapse the redirect chain.

findings.summary: Pages omit structured data for their catalog content.
findings.evidence: The metadata probe found zero JSON-LD blocks. Open Graph tags exist, but movie/listing entities are not expressed as schema.org data.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate JSON-LD for WebSite, SearchAction, BreadcrumbList, and Movie/TVSeries detail entities.

findings.summary: Essential security headers are absent.
findings.evidence: The headers probe found no CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options/frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy.
findings.suggestedFix: Set HSTS, nosniff, a restrictive CSP including frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy, and a minimal Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: Tracking and advertising execute before any user choice.
findings.evidence: Tracker evidence found Google Tag Manager and Google Analytics; the download template additionally injects several ad networks, tracking pixels, a hidden iframe, and an external player.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimise third parties, require explicit consent where applicable, sandbox necessary embeds, and document purposes/retention.

findings.summary: The site lacks browser-enforced containment for risky third-party code.
findings.evidence: No CSP/frame-ancestors/referrer/permissions policy is present while download pages execute numerous external scripts and embed cross-origin frames.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a nonce/hash-based CSP, strict frame and referrer controls, and isolate or remove untrusted advertising code.

findings.summary: The 404 response offers no route back or recovery action.
findings.evidence: A representative missing URL returns HTTP 404 with only “Not Found” and no search, home link, retry, or related content.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve a branded, lightweight 404 with search, home navigation, and recovery guidance.

findings.summary: The global/multilingual claim is not matched by direction-safe styling.
findings.evidence: Pages declare en/en-in, but CSS/DOM inspection found no logical sizing or spacing properties and no alternate language signals; physical left/right rules are widespread.
findings.suggestedFix: Use logical properties, preserve valid lang/dir per localized page, and publish hreflang only for real translations.

findings.summary: Download controls conceal side effects and hidden advertising surfaces.
findings.evidence: Several links labelled as direct quality downloads open an unrelated ad URL, and an opacity 0.001 fixed iframe is inserted behind the page.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove hidden frames and popup side effects; use honest labels and explicit, user-initiated external actions.

findings.summary: The search form provides no humane invalid-input feedback.
findings.evidence: Submitting an empty search is intercepted and returns false without a message, aria-invalid state, or focus guidance.
findings.suggestedFix: Use native constraints and show an accessible error after interaction, announced via a live region.

findings.summary: The search input omits basic input assistance metadata.
findings.evidence: The input has no name, autocomplete, inputmode, or accessible label, reducing browser and assistive support.
findings.suggestedFix: Give the query field a stable name, autocomplete value appropriate to search, and labelled search semantics.

findings.summary: Image delivery wastes substantial bandwidth.
findings.evidence: All 77 audited images use legacy formats, 36 are oversized, 37 lack srcset, and HAR attributes 2.25 MB to images.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate responsive AVIF/WebP sources and right-size each cover/logo for its rendered slot.

findings.summary: The page fetches work users have not requested.
findings.evidence: Seventy-four below-fold images load eagerly and analytics starts during initial load; most of the 2.43 MB transfer is offscreen content.
findings.suggestedFix: Lazy-load offscreen assets and defer nonessential analytics/background work until idle and consented.

findings.summary: There is no effective third-party or page-weight budget.
findings.evidence: The starting URL causes 46 requests classified off the original origin after a four-host chain, plus analytics; download pages add multiple ad/player origins.
findings.suggestedFix: Set enforceable page-weight and third-party budgets, consolidate the host, and remove nonessential ad/analytics dependencies.

taskList.title: Remove hidden advertising surfaces and undisclosed popup side effects from download links
Collapse the multi-domain redirect chain and align canonical and sitemap URLs
Lazy-load and right-size responsive modern-format cover images
Deploy CSP, HSTS, nosniff, frame, referrer, and permissions policies
Fix the search field label, contrast, validation, and assistance metadata
Modernise the request template for mobile reflow and usable targets
Minimise and consent-gate analytics and other third parties
